findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on undefined method '[]' for nil whenever the embed_category site setting has never been explicitly set (the default is ''). On any fresh install — and on existing sites that never configured embed_category — `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]` returns nil because non-default site settings have no row, so `[0]['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError and the deploy's db:migrate aborts; every test database bootstrap also fails.

[BUG] The update action ignores its params and persists nothing, making PUT /admin/customize/embedding a silent no-op while still returning a success serialization. The frontend admin-embedding controller's saveChanges() calls embedding.update({}), which PUTs to this endpoint; the admin sees the request succeed but no setting is ever written — any embedding configuration edits are silently dropped.

[BUG] The update action passes a nil host to save_host when no EmbeddableHost matches params[:id], crashing on nil.host=. A PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id (e.g. after the row was deleted in another tab) returns a 500 NoMethodError instead of the 404 the admin API contract implies; destroy has the same nil.destroy crash.

[ADVISORY] Host values from the old site setting are interpolated directly into a raw SQL INSERT string inside a `change` migration. Any host value containing a quote (or a hand-edited embeddable_hosts setting) breaks the migration with a SQL syntax error; data-only work inside `change` also makes the migration silently non-reversible, so `rake db:rollback` drops the table and permanently destroys the migrated host data with no way to restore it.

[ADVISORY] save_host reads params[:embeddable_host][:host] without any presence check, and the Ember model sends the payload only if the admin route's serializer nesting matches. An update/create request whose params lack the embeddable_host key (empty body, API client, or a record where the host field was never filled) raises NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of a 4xx validation error — combined with the model's format validation this means empty hosts hit the server crash path before the validation can render render_json_error.

[ADVISORY] The before_validation callback uses sub!/ on the host attribute, which mutates in place and silently skips when the string is frozen or the pattern doesn't match the expected position. A host like 'https://example.com' entered via the API (not the admin UI) is stripped by sub! correctly, but a host with a leading capital scheme 'HTTPS://example.com' fails both the regex validation and the strip, producing a confusing validation error rather than normalization; the in-place mutation also means a failed save leaves the caller's object already mutated.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any site that has no 'embed_category' row in site_settings (fresh installs or sites that never configured embedding), because execute(...)[0] is nil and ['id'] is called on it. db:migrate fails mid-deployment for sites without the embed_category setting, blocking upgrades entirely.

[BUG] The migration interpolates raw site-setting values directly into INSERT SQL ("INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."), so any embeddable_hosts entry containing a quote or SQL metacharacter breaks or corrupts the migration. The operator whose embeddable_hosts setting contains an entry like "eviltrout's site" gets a failed/half-applied migration; unescaped interpolation is also a SQL injection vector for whatever wrote that setting.

[BUG] update and destroy do a where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil check, then call methods on the result, so a stale/unknown id raises NoMethodError (nil.host= / nil.destroy) and returns a 500. An admin double-clicking delete or saving a row already deleted by another session gets a 500 error instead of a 404/422; the spec file adds no coverage for this path.

[BUG] The update action persists nothing — it re-fetches the OpenStruct and re-renders it — so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint the frontend saveChanges action calls is an inert no-op. The 'saveChanges' action in admin-embedding.js.es6 silently succeeds while changing nothing; an admin who edits anything on that page believes it saved. The controller spec only asserts the subclass relationship, so this dead behavior is unverified.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import now derives the category solely from EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url), and when no host record matches the URL it passes category: nil, silently dropping the previous SiteSetting.embed_category behavior with no fallback or guard. Feed polling or embedding from a URL whose host has no EmbeddableHost record (e.g. before the admin adds it, or a feed URL on a different host than the embeddable page host) creates topics in Uncategorized instead of a configured category; no spec covers the no-matching-host branch.

[BUG] The model has no uniqueness validation or unique index on host, so duplicate host rows can be created via the admin UI with different or differently-cased spellings. An admin saving 'eviltrout.com' twice gets two rows; record_for_host returns an arbitrary one, so the category mapping is nondeterministic with no error surfaced at save time. The migration also creates the table without a unique index.

[BUG] The only controller spec asserts the class's superclass and never exercises create, update, destroy, the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id, or the validation-error path. The core behaviors of this new controller (including the nil-id 500 above and the render_json_error contract) have zero test coverage; a regression in save_host ships undetected.

[BUG] The embedding controller spec only checks inheritance and never asserts that show returns the host list or that update persists anything, which is exactly why the inert update action went unnoticed. The serialization contract (root: 'embedding', embed: :ids consumed by the store's new plural _ids hydration) is unverified end-to-end; the store hydration change is tested only against the fruits fixture, not against the real embedding payload.

[ADVISORY] before_validation strips scheme and path but keeps any port, while record_for_host compares URI#host (which excludes the port), so a host saved with a port (e.g. 'localhost:3000', which the regex permits) can never match a referer. The admin who enters localhost:3000 to allow dev embedding gets a row that host_allowed? never matches, with no error at save or check time.

[ADVISORY] The delete action's destroyRecord() promise has no .catch, so a failed server delete leaves the row in the table with no error surfaced to the admin. An admin on a flaky connection sees nothing happen on delete failure and retries, while the row remains; contrast with save() which does handle popupAjaxError.

[ADVISORY] create_table uses force: true, which silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table and its data if the migration is re-run or a plugin already defined the table. A site with a prior table of that name loses its host rows without warning during migration.

[BUG] expandable_first_post? silently drops the embeddable-hosts presence check, changing behavior for sites with no hosts configured. On a site with an empty embeddable_hosts table and embed_truncate enabled, any topic with a topic embed now returns expandable_first_post? true where it previously returned false; the topic list renders the expand affordance for embeds whose host no longer exists, and the removed spec case ('is false if embeddable_host is blank') is deleted rather than ported, so nothing pins the old contract.

[ADVISORY] The update action is a no-op that serializes the same unmodified OpenStruct, yet the client exposes a saveChanges button wired to it. An admin clicks save on the embedding screen, gets a success response, and nothing is persisted — the Embedding model has no editable attributes, so both the PUT route and the controller's saveChanges action are dead code that will mislead the next developer into thinking embedding-level settings exist here; the route, controller action, and client action should be deleted until there is something to update.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import now assigns category nil when the URL's host has no EmbeddableHost record, removing any traceable default behavior without a replacement. Feed polling (topic_retriever → TopicEmbed.import) for a URL whose host is not in the table — e.g. any host configured before the migration data backfill edge cases, or a feed URL on a subdomain not exactly matching a stored host — creates uncategorized topics instead of a configured category; note this path is the invalid_host? guard's complement but category nil here diverges from the controller's explicit fallback to uncategorized_category_id, so two entry points now disagree on the default.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes category_fabricator.rb's contents and re-creates them inside embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, inverting the file names relative to their contents. Every future contributor running grep for 'Fabricator(:category)' lands in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, and any new category fabricator added to category_fabricator.rb (now holding only embeddable_host) fragments across two misleadingly named files; the fabricators should live in files matching their names.

[ADVISORY] The generic store's _hydrateEmbedded is extended with plural *_ids hydration (plus matching pretender fixture and test changes) purely to serve this feature's embedding serializer, expanding shared framework surface beyond the stated scope. Every Ember model hydrating through the store now runs the new regex branch /(.+)\_id(s?)$/ against every payload key; any existing API that happens to send a key ending in _ids (e.g. moderator_ids on user payloads) silently gains new hydration behavior without an audit of existing payloads in this diff — the feature could have used the existing singular embed pattern or sideloaded the hosts directly, avoiding a core-store change for one admin screen.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim, with no scheme/path stripping or downcasing, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against a bare URI#host. Any site whose old setting contained values like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (both explicitly supported and tested in the old setting code, and used in the updated embed_controller_spec) gets rows stored as 'http://discourse.org'/'https://example.com/1234'; the before_validation normalization never runs on raw SQL inserts, so every subsequent embed request from those hosts is rejected with InvalidAccess — the migration silently disables embedding for exactly the hosts it was meant to preserve.

[BUG] The migration calls [0]['id'].to_i on the embed_category query result without checking that a row was returned. On any install where the embed_category site setting is empty or does not match a category name (the common case — default is ''), the SQL returns zero rows, execute(...)[0] is nil, and the migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil['id'], aborting the deploy's migration run.

[BUG] update and destroy call methods directly on the result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without a nil check. A PUT or DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id (e.g. after another admin deleted the row) makes save_host(nil) or nil.destroy raise NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of the 404 the REST contract implies.

[ADVISORY] The model has no uniqueness validation and the table has no unique index on host, so duplicate host rows are representable. Two admins (or a double-clicked save) create two 'eviltrout.com' rows with different categories; record_for_host returns .first by arbitrary order, so embedded topics silently land in whichever category happens to sort first, and the embedding admin UI shows two visually identical rows whose edit/delete results are non-deterministic.

[ADVISORY] before_validation normalizes only the leading scheme and path, but the validation regex accepts a :port suffix, and lookup compares against URI#host which strips the port. An admin who enters 'example.com:8080' (accepted by the regex) creates a record that can never match any referer, since record_for_host extracts 'example.com' without the port; the host is stored and displayed as allowed but every embed request from it is rejected.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host does a full-table linear scan via lower(host) = ? with no index on lower(host) (or host) anywhere in the migration. This runs on every embed/comments request (embed_controller#ensure_embeddable, a hot anonymous-accessible path); with a growing host list the lookup is O(n) per request, and the case-insensitive predicate can't use a plain btree on host even if one existed later.

[ADVISORY] The update action never reads params or mutates anything — it only re-renders the same OpenStruct that fetch_embedding already loaded. PUT /admin/customize/embedding always returns 200 while persisting nothing; the client saveChanges action (embedding.update({})) appears to save but is a silent no-op, so any future per-embedding setting routed through this endpoint will silently fail to persist while reporting success.

[ADVISORY] Legacy host strings are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL with no quoting/escaping. A legacy embeddable_hosts value containing a single quote (or a value the setting UI allowed) breaks the INSERT with a SQL syntax error, aborting the migration; the same backfill path also never runs the model's normalization, which is the root of the stored-format drift found above.

[ADVISORY] create_table uses force: true, dropping any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table before recreating it. Running the migration against a database where this table was already created (e.g. a re-run or a partially-migrated shard) silently destroys all host/category mappings with no backfill from site_settings (which the same migration then deletes), leaving embedding permanently unlocked-unconfigured.

[ADVISORY] The save action does not commit the buffer (no this.commitBuffer() / buffer.applyBufferedChanges), it reads buffered properties manually and then hand-sets host.category from a client-side Category.findById lookup after save. After a save succeeds, the underlying host record's 'host' attribute still holds the pre-edit value (only the server copy changed), so any later rollbackBuffer/cancel or a render reading host.host instead of the buffered value shows the stale hostname; the hand-maintained category association is a second copy of state the server response already returns, which will drift the first time someone edits a field not covered by getProperties('host').

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any site where the embed_category setting is unset (its default is ''). `SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` matches no row when the setting value is blank, so `execute(...)[0]` is nil and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the deploy's migration for every default install.

[BUG] expandable_first_post? silently dropped the embeddable-hosts-present guard, changing behavior for sites with no hosts configured. Previously a site with blank embeddable_hosts never truncated/expanded first posts; after this change any topic with a topic_embed and embed_truncate enabled (e.g. created via DiscourseConnect feed embedding, which never required embeddable_hosts) will expand/truncate regardless of host configuration — a behavior change outside the PR's stated intent of editing host/category relationships.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update accepts a PUT and returns success while persisting nothing — it re-renders the fetched OpenStruct without applying any params. The client's saveChanges action (admin-embedding.js.es6 saveChanges) PUTs to /admin/customize/embedding and shows no error, but the operation is a silent no-op; an admin believing they saved embedding settings is bitten whenever a future field is added to this form. Either wire the update or drop the route/action until it does something.

[ADVISORY] Migrated host values are interpolated directly into raw SQL INSERTs. A previously-saved embeddable_hosts value containing a single quote (the old setting was free-text host_list) raises a SQL syntax error or corrupts the insert during migration, leaving the site half-migrated with site_settings already deleted; use quote/parameterized inserts.

[ADVISORY] The distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error condition was collapsed into 'invalid referer host'. An admin debugging an embed that returns 403 on a site where no hosts exist (fresh migration produced an empty table) now sees the misleading 'invalid referer host' message instead of the explicit not-configured message, masking the actual misconfiguration.

[ADVISORY] The migration string-interpolates the raw `embeddable_hosts` site setting value directly into an INSERT statement. Any host entry containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacters) breaks the INSERT or executes arbitrary SQL during migration; the value comes from an admin-editable site setting that was never validated against the new host format regex, so an operator upgrading with e.g. `eviltrout.com'; --` stored in the old setting gets a failed or corrupted migration.

[ADVISORY] The entire spec for the new CRUD controller asserts only `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`, verifying inheritance and nothing about behavior. Checked spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb — neither contains a single request. The create/update/destroy happy paths, the `render_json_error` validation-failure path, and the blank-category_id→uncategorized fallback in `save_host` all ship with zero behavioral coverage; a regression in `save_host` (e.g. dropping the category_id assignment or the blank fallback) passes the suite green, and admins get silent data corruption of host/category mappings.

[BUG] `update` and `destroy` call `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then use the result without a nil check, so a nonexistent or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. A double-delete from the admin UI (two admins, stale row) or a stale PUT sends id that no longer exists; `save_host(nil)` executes `nil.host = ...` and the request crashes with a 500 instead of a 404. The new spec file (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb) contains no request test, so this branch is never exercised by the diff.

[ADVISORY] The only TopicEmbed.import test covering the new per-host category logic runs with a valid embeddable_host and asserts the happy path; the new `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url); category: eh.try(:category_id)` branch where no host matches is never exercised. When the embedded URL's host is not in EmbeddableHost (previously TopicRetriever guaranteed a match, but TopicEmbed.import is a public API also called from feeds where `invalid_host?` is checked only in TopicRetriever), `record_for_host` returns false and `category` becomes nil instead of the removed `SiteSetting.embed_category` — imported topics land in no category. A regression to this fallback (e.g. defaulting to uncategorized) would be invisible to the suite; I checked spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb and no test imports with a URL whose host is absent.

[ADVISORY] The model spec covers only the host-trimming happy path and host_allowed? lookups; the format validation's rejection branch (`validates_format_of`) and case-insensitive matching between stored and requested hosts are never tested. The regex accepts things like 'example.com/anything' after trimming but the trimming mutates via `sub!` on the attribute — a regression in `before_validation` (e.g. `sub!` on a frozen or nil host, or a pattern that stops stripping) would go unnoticed. Checked spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb: there is no `expect(eh).not_to be_valid` case, so invalid input handling (e.g. 'not_a_host', empty string) is unverified; admins can save garbage hosts via the new controller and the embed allowlist silently never matches.

[ADVISORY] `update` re-serializes `@embedding` without applying any params, so it is a no-op that returns success regardless of what the client PUTs, and no test detects this because spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb never issues a request. The admin UI's saveChanges action PUTs to /customize/embedding and receives a 200 with unchanged data — the UI appears to save but nothing persists. The spec file's subclass-only assertion (lines 4–8) passes identically whether update works or not; I checked spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb and it contains no update test.

[BUG] The embed_category lookup crashes with NoMethodError when the site_settings table has no 'embed_category' row, aborting the migration mid-deploy. Sites that never set embed_category (default is '' and the row may not exist in site_settings) make `execute(...)[0]` return nil, so `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError on nil, and the migration plus the entire deploy fails on every `db:migrate`. The same nil-crash applies to the uncategorized_category_id fallback on line 13.

[BUG] The backfill inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim without stripping the http(s):// prefix or path, but EmbeddableHost#record_for_host compares stored values to a bare URI host, so migrated rows never match. A site whose setting was 'http://eviltrout.com' (a form the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly supported — its own tests set it that way) gets a row stored as 'http://eviltrout.com'; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host does `where("lower(host) = ?", 'eviltrout.com')` and finds nothing, so embedding checks and TopicEmbed.import category lookup silently fail for every pre-existing host after the migration, and then the original setting is DELETEd — the admin's data is gone with no way to recover it.

[BUG] The migration unconditionally DELETEs the 'embeddable_hosts' and 'embed_category' site settings even when no rows were successfully migrated, inside a `change` method whose raw SQL has no reversible counterpart. Any site where the embeddable_hosts value is blank, or where the INSERTs fail/skip, still loses its embed_category setting (which carried a category name not otherwise migrated anywhere), and a rollback (`db:rollback`) drops the table but cannot restore the deleted settings — the migration is irreversible and destroys source data with no backup/export step.

[ADVISORY] Backfill values are string-interpolated directly into INSERT SQL with no parameterization or model-layer normalization, unlike every other write path which routes through EmbeddableHost's before_validation stripping. Any legacy setting value containing a quote or newline breaks the INSERT (or writes junk rows the model layer would have cleaned), leaving partially migrated data before the DELETE runs — operators get hosts that are malformed and can never be re-imported because the source setting row is then destroyed.

[ADVISORY] The embed_category lookup matches category by exact name string from the setting value, with no fallback if the category was renamed or the setting holds an id instead of a name. Sites where the admin renamed the category after setting embed_category get every host silently assigned to the uncategorized fallback, and since the original setting is deleted at line 31 the original mapping is unrecoverable.

[BUG] update with a nonexistent or deleted host id passes nil into save_host, which calls host.host = ... on nil and raises NoMethodError, returning a raw 500 where a 404/4xx belongs. An admin editing a host that was concurrently deleted by another admin gets an unhandled 500 with a stack trace in logs, instead of a clean not-found error; same unguarded nil pattern repeats in destroy (line 16).

[BUG] The update action renders success_json-shaped serialized output without saving anything, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint always reports success while persisting zero changes. The admin UI's saveChanges() (admin-embedding.js.es6 line 7: this.get('embedding').update({})) resolves as a successful save with no error surfaced, leaving any future embedding settings silently unmodified — a silent no-op reported as success.

[BUG] destroyRecord().then(...) has no .catch, so a failed DELETE (network error, 500) is an unhandled promise rejection with no error surfaced to the admin. When the destroy request fails, the host silently stays in the server DB but the admin sees no feedback at all — no popup, no console error handled — and the row appears unchanged with no explanation, unlike the save() path which does catch and popupAjaxError.

[BUG] The new plural branch calls obj[k].map without a null guard, so a payload where a *_ids key is null (serializer emits null for an empty has_many) throws TypeError: Cannot read property 'map' of null during hydration. Any REST-serializer response carrying e.g. "embeddable_host_ids": null (or a null plural foreign key) crashes hydration of the whole payload, breaking the admin embedding page load for that record instead of rendering an empty list.

[ADVISORY] saveChanges calls embedding.update({}) with no error handler, so even if update were wired to save, a server rejection would be a silent unhandled rejection. Admin clicking save on the embedding screen gets no feedback on failure; combined with the server-side update being a no-op, the whole save flow is invisible-failure by construction.

[ADVISORY] Save sets host.category from Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) after the server round-trip, and findById returns null/undefined for an unknown id with no guard, so the saved row displays a blank category badge until reload. When the chosen category is not in the client-side category list (e.g., a restricted category the admin can't see), the just-saved host renders with no category even though the server stored category_id correctly; also no in-flight guard beyond isSaving prevents double-click double-submit on the save action itself.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
